preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**3 and 1 <= m <= 10**3 for n, m in [(int(stdin.split()[0]), int(stdin.split()[1]))])
preconditions.description: Input dimensions n and m are integers between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) == m and all(c in {'D', 'I', 'M', 'A'} for c in line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The table consists of exactly n lines, each containing exactly m characters, all of which are in {'D', 'I', 'M', 'A'}.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Poor Dima!' if not any('D' in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) else None
postconditions.description: If no 'D' exists in the table, output 'Poor Dima!' (no traversal possible).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Poor Inna!' if any('D' in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and any(cycle_exists(table) for table in [stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) else None
postconditions.description: If there exists a cycle (infinite traversal) starting from any 'D', output 'Poor Inna!' (infinite traversal possible).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().isdigit() and int(stdout.strip()) == max(max_traversals(table) for table in [stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) if any('D' in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and not any(cycle_exists(table) for table in [stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) else None
postconditions.description: If no infinite cycle exists but at least one traversal is possible, output the maximum number of times 'DIMA' can be traversed, starting from any 'D'.
